gloss: Chūshingura; the story of the 47 rōnin

definitions.explanation: The story of the 47 masterless samurai of the Akō domain who in 1702 avenged their lord's forced suicide by killing the official they blamed, and were then ordered to commit suicide themselves. The name comes from the 1748 puppet and kabuki play {仮名手本忠臣蔵|かなでほんちゅうしんぐら}, and it now covers all retellings in film, television, and fiction.

examples.japanese: ⟦{年末|ねんまつ}→年末：17688_nenmatsu⟧になると{忠臣蔵|ちゅうしんぐら}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{思|おも}い{出|だ}す→思い出す：01258_omoidasu⟧。
examples.english: When the end of the year comes, I think of Chūshingura.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{忠臣蔵|ちゅうしんぐら}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ドラマ→ドラマ：03867_dorama⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大好|だいす}き→大好き：02911_daisuki⟧だ。
{忠臣蔵|ちゅうしんぐら}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{浪士|ろうし}たちは、⟦{雪|ゆき}→雪：00584_yuki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{吉良邸|きらてい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{討|う}ち{入|い}った。
examples.english: The rōnin of Chūshingura raided Kira's mansion on a snowy night.

notes:
The raid took place on the 14th day of the 12th month, so the story is a traditional year-end staple on television and in theaters. It is the classic Japanese tale of loyalty and revenge.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {赤穂浪士|あこうろうし}: the Akō rōnin, the historical name for the 47
- {四十七士|しじゅうしちし}: the forty-seven samurai
- {討|う}ち{入|い}り: the raid on {吉良上野介|きらこうずけのすけ}'s mansion
- {殿中|でんちゅう}でござる: "You are in the palace!" — the cry when their lord drew his sword inside Edo Castle, jokingly used to stop someone losing their temper

CULTURAL NOTE:
The leader {大石内蔵助|おおいしくらのすけ} pretended to live a dissolute life to throw off suspicion before the attack, and his name stands for patient, hidden resolve.
